_about: History-driven price changes (design.md section 11.3, research.md section 8). The multiplier fades linearly from mul_start to mul_end across the dates.

sources: Harris (1839) ch. II: the war 'trebled the price of every thing, and of live stock in particular'; oxen still 'considered high' at 45 Rds in Dec 1838 (Backhouse). Base ox price already includes the war rise; this adds a small extra early in 1837 (invented).
Potgieter lost 5,000 sheep, 300 cattle and 100 draught oxen at Vegkop, Oct 1836 (SA Military History). Multiplier invented.
Meal at Colesberg 75s a muid, June 1839, against an 'old price' of 6-10 Rds (Backhouse). The cause is not recorded; the rise over 1837-39 is invented.
